q: 351. The minimum clear horizontal spacing between groups of cables or ducts of grouped cables shall be greater of
options: 30 mm or 5 mm more than maximum size of aggregate
40 mm or 5 mm more than maximum size of aggregate
30 mm or maximum size of aggregate
40 mm or maximum size of aggregate
explain: The code requires the minimum clear horizontal spacing between groups/ducts of grouped cables to be the greater of 40 mm or 5 mm more than the maximum aggregate size, to permit proper concrete placement.

q: 352. The minimum clear vertical spacing between groups of cables or ducts of grouped cables shall be
explain: For grouped cables/ducts, the code specifies a minimum clear vertical spacing of 50 mm between groups to ensure adequate concrete cover and compaction.

q: 353. The grouting of ducts in post-tensioned prestressed concrete causes
explain: Grouting bonds the tendon to the surrounding concrete, which improves load transfer (reducing deflection and crack width) while also protecting the tendon from corrosion — all benefits occur together.

q: 354. A parabolic tendon in prestressed beam causes an equivalent balancing
explain: A parabolic tendon profile produces a uniformly varying upward transverse force along its length, which acts as an equivalent distributed load balancing the external gravity loads on the beam.

q: 355. An increase in strain in a concrete member at constant stress is called
explain: Creep is defined as the gradual increase in strain in concrete under a sustained constant stress over time.

q: 356. Strain in concrete at zero stress is called
explain: Shrinkage is the volumetric/strain change that occurs in concrete due to moisture loss even in the absence of any applied stress.

q: 357. In case of prestressed concrete, prestressing force is
explain: Prestressing induces a compressive force in the concrete section (via tensioned tendons) so that tensile stresses from external loads are counteracted.

q: 358. In case of prestressed concrete
options: load carrying capacity of member increases
quantity of concrete is saved for same grade
quantity of steel is saved for same grade
explain: Prestressing utilizes the full section more efficiently, so it increases load-carrying capacity while also economizing on both concrete and steel quantities compared to ordinary RCC — all these benefits occur.

q: 359. Light weight concrete is prepared by
options: formation of air void in concrete by omitting sand
formation of air voids in cement paste by the substances causing foam
explain: Light weight concrete can be produced using lightweight aggregates, by omitting fine aggregate (no-fines concrete), or by introducing air voids through foaming agents — all these are recognized methods.

q: 360. Light weight concrete is used in
explain: Because of its lower strength and density, light weight concrete finds its principal application in non-load-bearing wall construction such as partition walls.

q: 361. To obtain a light weight concrete the types of aggregate used is
explain: Pumice is a naturally occurring porous, low-density volcanic aggregate commonly used to produce light weight concrete.

q: 362. A concrete in which dry coarse aggregate are first packed to have the least voids and then the cement sand mortar is injected under pressure to fill all the voids, resulting in a very dense concrete, is known as
explain: This describes pre-packed concrete, where coarse aggregate is placed first and mortar is then grouted under pressure into the voids to produce a dense mass.

q: 363. The ferrocement is a composite material obtained by
options: random disposal of short, discontinuous fibres in the conventional concrete
reinforcing the cement mortar with steel fibres in the form of wire mesh
blending ferrous compounds in the ordinary Portland cement
explain: Ferrocement is defined as cement mortar reinforced with closely spaced layers of continuous, relatively thin steel wire mesh, distinguishing it from randomly dispersed fibre-reinforced concrete.

q: 364. The cement sand ratio in the ferrocement matrix should not be leaner than
explain: To achieve adequate strength and to properly encase the closely spaced wire mesh, the ferrocement matrix cement-sand ratio should not be leaner than 1:2.5.

q: 365. The volume of reinforcement in ferrocement (percent) normally varies between
explain: In typical ferrocement construction, the volume fraction of the wire mesh reinforcement generally lies in the range of 5% to 8% of the total volume.

q: 366. The water cement ratio for ferrocement mix should be
explain: A relatively low water-cement ratio of 0.35 to 0.40 is recommended for ferrocement mixes so that the rich mortar can properly penetrate the closely spaced mesh while maintaining strength.

q: 367. What is the process of smoothening the surface of newly placed concrete with a trowel called?
explain: The operation of smoothening and levelling the surface of freshly placed concrete is termed floating, carried out with a float/trowel before final finishing.

q: 368. If water cement ratio is more,
options: the durability of the concrete will be more
the durability of the concrete will be less
the durability of the concrete will not be affected
explain: A higher water-cement ratio increases the porosity and permeability of hardened concrete, which reduces its durability against attack by external agents.

q: 369. Low water-cement ratio in concrete:
options: improves the frost resistance of concrete
explain: A low water-cement ratio produces a denser paste, which simultaneously lowers permeability, raises compressive strength, and improves resistance to frost/freeze-thaw damage.

q: 370. To get ultra high strength concrete :
options: compaction by pressure and helical binding
explain: Ultra high strength concretes are produced using several specialized techniques — pressure compaction with helical confinement, polymer impregnation, and reactive powder concrete technology — so all listed methods apply.

q: 371. As compared to Ordinary Portland Cement, use of pozzolanic cement:
explain: Pozzolanic cement reacts with liberated calcium hydroxide to form additional cementitious compounds over time, resulting in increased long-term strength compared to OPC.

q: 372. Steel mould used for slump test is in the form of :
explain: The standard slump test mould is a frustum of a cone (Abrams cone), which is filled with concrete and lifted vertically to measure the resulting slump.

q: 373. The interval for which the cement products remain in plastic condition is known as::
explain: Setting time refers to the period during which the cement paste remains workable/plastic before it begins to stiffen and lose plasticity.

q: 374. The compressive strength of an ordinary Portland cement (1:3::Cement:sand) after seven days test should not be less than:
explain: As per Indian Standard specifications for OPC mortar cubes (1:3), the minimum 7-day compressive strength requirement is 175 kg/cm².

q: 375. The concrete in which preliminary tests are preformed for designing the mix is called:
explain: Controlled concrete refers to concrete whose mix proportions are determined and controlled through preliminary laboratory tests to meet specified strength and durability requirements.

q: 376. Concreting should be stopped when temperature falls below …
explain: Concreting operations are generally stopped once the ambient temperature drops below about 4.5°C, since hydration slows drastically and frost damage risk increases.

q: 377. Humidity causes ……… of cement in bag .
explain: Moisture in humid air can react with cement stored in bags, initiating premature hydration/setting reactions that spoil the cement before use.

q: 378. The purpose of reinforcement in prestressed concrete is :
options: to impact initial compressive stress in concrete
explain: The prestressing steel is tensioned specifically to impart an initial compressive stress into the concrete section before service loads are applied, which is the primary purpose in prestressed members.

q: 379. Reduction in aggregate - cement ratio while keeping W/C ratio constant causes :
explain: Reducing the aggregate-cement ratio means using more cement paste relative to aggregate, which, at the same water-cement ratio, provides more lubrication and thus increases workability.

q: 380. Modulus of rupture of concrete is measure of :
explain: Modulus of rupture is obtained from a beam flexure test and represents the flexural (bending) tensile strength of concrete.

q: 381. Slump test is done for
explain: The slump test is a standard field test specifically used to measure the workability/consistency of fresh concrete.

q: 382. The durability of concrete is proportion to :
explain: Durability of concrete is closely linked to the cement-aggregate ratio, since it governs the density and impermeability of the paste matrix surrounding the aggregate.

q: 383. Plain cement concrete is strong in taking :
explain: Plain (unreinforced) concrete has high compressive strength but is comparatively weak in tension and shear, hence it is primarily used to resist compressive stress.

q: 384. The removal of excess air after placing concrete helps in increasing the strength of concrete by :
explain: Proper compaction that removes entrapped/excess air from freshly placed concrete has been found to increase its strength by roughly 15 to 20%.

q: 385. The strength of concrete increase with decreases in :
explain: Strength of concrete is inversely related to the water-cement ratio — as the water-cement ratio decreases, the paste becomes denser and strength increases (Abrams' law).

q: 386. The cold bent test is conducted in a steel bar to determine :
explain: The cold bend test checks the ductility of reinforcement bars by bending a test specimen through a specified angle, typically 90 degrees, without cracking.

q: 387. As compared to ordinary Portland cement, use of pozzuloanic cement :
explain: Pozzolanic cement, through its secondary pozzolanic reaction with calcium hydroxide, results in improved long-term strength compared with ordinary Portland cement.

q: 388. For the same design load, the weight of concrete in a prestressed concrete as compared to ordinary reinforced concrete is less by :
explain: Because prestressed members use the full section more efficiently by pre-compressing the concrete, they require considerably less concrete — typically about 50% less — than an equivalent ordinary RCC member for the same load.

q: 389. To determine the modulus of rupture, the size of test specimen used is
explain: The standard flexural (modulus of rupture) test specimen for concrete is a beam of size 150 x 150 x 700 mm as per Indian Standard specifications.

q: 390. The steel mould used for slump test is in the form of :
explain: As with the standard slump test mould, it is shaped as a frustum of a cone (Abrams cone) open at both ends.

q: 391. Expansive cement expands mostly during its :
explain: Expansive cement is engineered so that most of its expansion occurs during the final hardening period, after initial set, to compensate for later drying shrinkage.

q: 392. Soundness of the material means the resistance of the material against the effect of :
explain: Soundness specifically refers to a material's ability to resist volume changes/deterioration from repeated cycles of freezing and thawing.

q: 393. What is a graded aggregate ?
options: it has particles of all sizes
it has particles between 4 mm - 6 mm
it has particles between 10 mm - 15 mm
it has particles between 2 mm - 5 mm
explain: A graded aggregate is one containing a well-distributed range of particle sizes, from the largest down to the smallest, rather than being confined to a narrow size range.

q: 394. Finer grinding of cement
options: affects only the early development of strength
explain: Finer grinding increases the surface area available for hydration, which speeds up early reactions and therefore mainly boosts early-age strength development rather than the ultimate strength.

q: 395. The individual variation between test strength of sample should not be more than
explain: As per test acceptance criteria, the deviation of an individual test result from the average of the sample should not exceed ±15% of the average value.

q: 396. To obtain a very high strength concrete, use very fine grained :
explain: Very fine grained granite is used as a dense filler/aggregate material to help achieve very high strength concrete by densifying the microstructure.

q: 397. The percentage of voids in cement is approximately :
explain: Loose cement powder typically contains approximately 40% voids by volume between its particles.

q: 398. *The resistance of an aggregate to wear is known as :
explain: Abrasion resistance specifically measures an aggregate's ability to withstand surface wearing action, distinct from crushing or impact resistance.

q: 399. For the construction of cement concrete floor the maximum permissible sizes of aggregate is :
explain: For thin concrete floor toppings/finishes, the maximum permissible aggregate size is limited to 10 mm to allow a smooth, well-finished surface.

q: 400. Age factor for permissible compressive stress in concrete after six months is :
explain: Concrete continues to gain strength with age, so codes allow an age factor of 1.20 to be applied to the permissible compressive stress for concrete that is six months old.

q: 401. Fineness of cement is measured in unit of :
explain: Fineness of cement is expressed as specific surface area per unit mass (e.g., m²/kg), i.e., area/mass, since finer cement has more surface area per unit weight.

q: 402. The cement-sad ratio used in the compressive strength test of cement as per the Indian Standard Specification is :
explain: As per Indian Standard Specification, the compressive strength test of cement is performed using a standard mortar of cement-sand ratio 1:3.

q: 403. The initial setting time of lime-pozzolana, is :
explain: Lime-pozzolana mixtures set relatively slowly, with a specified minimum initial setting time of 120 minutes as per standard requirements.

q: 404. The rocks which are formed due to cooling of magma at a considerable depth from earth's surface are called
explain: Plutonic (intrusive) rocks form from magma that cools slowly at considerable depth below the earth's surface, producing coarse-grained crystalline rock.

q: 405. Depending on the chemical composition and mechanical properties, iron may be classified as
explain: Based on carbon content and resulting mechanical properties, iron/iron alloys are broadly classified into cast iron, wrought iron, and steel — covering all the listed types.
